method: Linux accounts for committed virtual memory rather than resident pages, so admission of a new mapping depends on the overcommit mode and on CommitLimit, both visible in /proc/meminfo. The RAM share available for commit is RAM multiplied by vm.overcommit_ratio and divided by 100, rounded half up to whole MiB, because the kernel works in pages and the tool reports whole MiB. In mode 2 (never overcommit) CommitLimit is that RAM share plus swap, and the kernel refuses a request that would push Committed_AS past it: the allocation fails with ENOMEM and nothing is killed. In mode 0 (heuristic) no arithmetic limit is enforced; the kernel only rejects obviously excessive requests, so the tool reports RAM plus swap as the reference ceiling at which the workload stops being supportable and labels anything above it as oversubscribed. In mode 1 (always overcommit) no limit exists, so the ceiling is reported for context only, required swap is not applicable, and any allocation is admitted while the OOM killer arbitrates once pages are touched. Committed after this request is current Committed_AS plus the new commit; headroom is the mode ceiling minus Committed_AS before and after; utilisation is committed after divided by the ceiling as a percentage to one decimal, reported as 100 % when the ceiling is zero and anything is committed; the largest request that still fits is the headroom before the request, floored at zero. The swap top-up needed to admit the request is the excess of committed memory over the RAM share (mode 2) or over RAM (mode 0) minus existing swap, floored at zero, because extra swap raises CommitLimit byte for byte. Verdict bands use the unrounded utilisation: refused in mode 2 when committed after exceeds the limit, oversubscribed in modes 0 and 1, tight from 85 %, watch from 70 %, otherwise healthy headroom. Inputs are whole MiB: RAM and swap 1-16,777,216 and 0-16,777,216, the overcommit ratio 1-100, Committed_AS 0-33,554,432 and the new commit 1-33,554,432; only mode 2 uses the ratio. This is a planning model of kernel accounting for a host you describe, not a reading of any host; it does not change sysctl values, and it ignores per-cgroup memory limits, memlock rlimits and hugetlb reservations. Everything runs in the browser.
